text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Egypt reiterates its support to Morocco over Western Sahara and hopes that conflict with Algeria over the issue will be overcome.

- Western Sahara in the limelight with possible appointment of a new U.N. envoy in the region while more countries withdraw recognition of the Saharan Arab Democratic Republic (SADR) claiming sovereignty over the region.
- President of parliament meets representatives from cities of Sebta and Melilla, enclaves held by Spain since the 16th century.
- James Baker, the former U.S. Secretary of State, could be next United Nations special envoy in Western Sahara.
- Banks agree to reduce interest rates by one point on loans to small and medium-sized firms after King Hassan advised them to do so in his throne speech.
- Protective measures should be set up to preserve local wheat production which could collapse in the face of cheap imports.
- Morocco is among first six countries which benefit from Russian technical assistance notably for building electrical plants, steel mills and other industrial sectors.
- Moroccan Association for the Support of the Palestinian Struggle urges Moroccans to intensify assistance.
- Liberalisation of wheat imports decided in haste endanger local production and makes it necessary to devise an agricultural policy.
- Recent convention between government and political parties to guarantee fairness of elections raises question of whether it will go beyond mere intention.
- Morocco's leading holding group, ONA, ponders new approach in agro-industry sector.
- Moroccan Stock Exchange starts new era with gradual introduction of electronic trading this week.
